thread:
maria.chen: CI failing on sampleapp e2e after the latest SDK publish — lots of 503s on staging when hitting /v1. anyone seeing this?
ci-bot: [CI] job test/sampleapp-e2e failed (exit 1) — logs: https://ci.redwood.local/builds/1957654321 (snippet attached)
jonah: I reproduced locally. Generated client no longer sets the Host header template we relied on in auth middleware.
ashley: wait — which change removed it? last regen changed server normalization IIRC.
maria.chen: regen diff shows the servers block got simplified. vendor extension x-default-host is gone.
samir: paste the minimal diff pls
maria.chen: ```diff
- servers:
-  - url: https://{subdomain}.api.redwood.ai
-    variables:
-      subdomain:
-        default: v1
+ servers:
+  - url: https://api.redwood.ai
```
jonah: yeah that will break clients that interpolate subdomain into Host for sig verification. auth layer expects Host="v1.api.redwood.ai" not "api.redwood.ai"
ashley: CI pattern was 401 -> retry -> 503, consistent with a missing/incorrect Host header on proxied auth checks.
samir: how did regen drop the template? our typegen post-processor normalizes servers for parity — maybe too aggressive on templated hosts.
maria.chen: I ran `yarn regen:openapi --local` and saw the same transformation. repro steps in the artifact.
ci-bot: [Artifact] regen-diff uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood.local/regen-diff-1957654321.txt
jonah: decision needed: revert the post-processor or patch the auth middleware to tolerate the new host?
ashley: semver/consequence: changing default host template changes client behavior — that is effectively breaking. Should we treat as a minor release (breaking change) and coordinate SDK teams?
maria.chen: ouch. pipeline will auto-publish multiple SDKs if we merge a regen PR. we need to coordinate otherwise customers get broken clients.
samir: proposed plan: rollback the post-processor commit in codegen, run full `yarn regen` across sdks, run sampleapp e2e, then publish a patch release that preserves server variables. If we must change behavior later, do it behind a config flag in a minor.
jonah: agree. For immediate safety, revert and publish a patch. Changelog should call out 'fix: preserve server variable template (prevents auth failures in sample apps)'.
ashley: small bikeshed: does this warrant a patch or minor bump? It's breaking if consumers relied on new behavior, but almost all clients assume the template. I'd go with patch (fix) if we truly only restored previous behavior; if we change API semantics, mark minor.
maria.chen: reading semver: restoring previous behavior == patch. but the change is already in a commit that could be pulled by external consumers. safer to mark as patch and include clear changelog and note in release PR to coordinate SDK teams.
samir: I'll block the auto-publish job for a few hours while we verify.
jonah: I'll prepare a regen+typegen run and attach diffs. commands I'll run: `git checkout -b fix/openapi-preserve-servers && git revert <post-processor-commit> && yarn regen && yarn typegen && yarn test:sampleapp:e2e`.
ashley: I'll open the release PR and set the changelog entry. PR title: "fix(openapi): preserve server variable templates to avoid auth regressions (regen revert)". In PR body I'll request delays on auto-publish actions and call out SDK owners.
deploy-bot: @channel release pipeline paused for 4 hours per request from devex (ticket DEVEX-1123).
maria.chen: assigning: @ashley open release PR, @jonah run regen + verify, @samir pause publish pipeline. I'll follow up with sampleapp e2e results here. :thumbsup:
